clue.text: Stimulant ordered with ecstasy just before deadline

indicators.note: things that are ordered are arranged afresh, so the letters are put into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone pops pills and party drugs to pull an all-nighter before a deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-minute thing happens at the latest possible moment, right before time runs out.

clue.text: See Director-General close to the gatehouse

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look
DG is the abbreviation for Director-General

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: An order to visit the head of the organisation near the gatehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small house at the gates of an estate, occupied by a gatekeeper.

clue.text: Case with crowd riotous in hallowed institution

indicators.note: a riotous crowd is out of control, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters of case and crowd rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal case triggers rioting crowds at a venerable establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idea or institution treated as beyond criticism, as if holy.

clue.text: Hill test for vehicle crossing French one

indicators.note: crossing means the test goes across and around the French word, enclosing it

parts.note: the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A road test checks a car can get over a hill and a French one too.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount is a word for a mountain or hill, as in place names like Mount Sinai.

clue.text: Brandy measure has bite

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small drink of spirits
second meaning: a small sharp bite or pinch

explanation.surface: A shot of brandy carries a kick.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a small tot of spirits, and to nip is to bite or pinch sharply.

clue.text: Team's leader assists securing a mountain range

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter

indicators.note: securing means the word for assists holds the article fast inside it

parts.note: helps means assists
taken as written

explanation.surface: The captain helps the climbing team secure a route up a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain range stretching across south-central Europe.

clue.text: One in Paris and Rome excited promoter

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so the city names are agitated into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the letters of the two cities rearranged

explanation.surface: A thrilled showbiz promoter is at work in two European capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and promotes concerts, operas or theatrical shows.

clue.text: Prominent Florentine family shortly finding doctor

indicators.note: said shortly, the family name is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: the Medici ruled Renaissance Florence

explanation.surface: A historian discovers a physician among the famous Florentine dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Medic is an informal word for a physician or other medical practitioner.

clue.text: MP given support in UN? Plenty!

indicators.note: in says the politician and the support sit inside the two letters for the world body

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A member of parliament enjoys plenty of backing at the United Nations.
explanation.walkthrough: Support is a golf tee here, not political backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for a large but unspecified number, so very many, plenty.

clue.text: Province not one area da Gama visits?

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the explorer's first name is placed within the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A question whether the Portuguese explorer ever visited this Canadian region.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints Vasco da Gama never got there, which is true; the letters for 'not one area' are split around him.
explanation.definitionFit: Nova Scotia is one of Canada's provinces, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Danced about etc when drunk returned to office

indicators.note: a drunk person's movements are jumbled, so these three letters come out scrambled
about means the dancing word goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: to reel is to dance a reel, a lively Scottish dance
the letters of etc rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician danced and so on while tipsy after winning the vote again.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters sit between REEL and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone re-elected is voted back into the post they already held.

clue.text: Five must leave Barking Advertiser: most depressing

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the remaining letters are crazily mixed up
something that must leave has to be taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
taken as written

explanation.surface: Five staff must quit the Barking Advertiser, a local paper in a dismal state.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, so the surface reads as its local newspaper; take V out of ADVERTISER before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreariest is the superlative of dreary, meaning dull and depressing.

clue.text: Ladies for example in Cromwell Avenue

indicators.note: in says the answer is sitting within the words of the street name that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A public toilet for women is found on a street named after Cromwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ladies is the British name for a women's public toilet; lav is short for lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' toilet is one kind of lavatory, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Rare fright catching cold

indicators.note: catching means the word for fright grabs and holds the letter for cold inside it

parts.note: a scare is a fright
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An unusual shock comes as one goes down with a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce and rare are synonyms: both mean in short supply or seldom found.

clue.text: Cunning writer Umberto pens note in style

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as in a pen, so the note is held inside

parts.note: art means craft or cunning
D is a musical note
Umberto Eco was the Italian author of The Name of the Rose

explanation.surface: The crafty novelist Umberto Eco writes a stylish note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like the writer's verb, but it means enclosing: the cunning word and the novelist together hold the note.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is a decorative style of the 1920s and 30s known for bold geometric forms.

clue.text: Against poetry being recited?

indicators.note: something recited is spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like it

parts.note: verses are lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone is opposed to poems being read out in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus is the Latin preposition used for one side opposed to another, as in a match or legal case.

clue.text: Creature leaving sinking ship? Sailor returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor heads back to port after an animal deserts a foundering vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying that rats desert a sinking ship, also used of disloyal people.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says rats are the first to flee a ship that is going down, so the animal fits.

clue.text: Wife playing pelota or game of pool?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being moved around in play into a new order

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
the letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A wife choosing between the Basque ball game pelota and a game of pool.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool here is a swimming pool, not the table game the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Water polo is a team ball game played in a swimming pool, hence a pool game.

clue.text: Inventive sort creates lakeside houses

indicators.note: houses means the words that follow contain the answer inside them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An imaginative person builds homes by the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was a celebrated inventor, pioneer of alternating current, so a person given to invention.

clue.text: One runs around wicket keeper

indicators.note: around means the number word goes round the cricket letter

parts.note: taken as written
W is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for wicket
R is the abbreviation for runs in cricket

explanation.surface: In cricket, a batter scampers around the wicketkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside ONE, then R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner keeps or possesses something, so is its keeper.

clue.text: Old Roman emperor seen with American heavy

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Nero was a first-century Roman emperor
US abbreviates United States, so American

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler of Rome is spotted alongside a weighty American.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous means burdensome, and a heavy task or duty is a burdensome one.

clue.text: Starts to observe Ulyssean traits in Bloom

parts.note: the first letters

explanation.walkthrough: Bloom is the hero of Joyce's Ulysses, so the capital disguises the gardening sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that are out have opened, meaning they are in bloom.

clue.text: Mean insulin to be used regularly for tiredness?

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at a steady interval, here every second one

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A diabetic is told to take a modest dose of insulin routinely to ward off fatigue.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits ennui is weariness of spirit more than physical tiredness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a jaded weariness, which the setter loosely likens to tiredness.

clue.text: Spar put in advertisement for email manager

indicators.note: put in says the pole word is placed inside the word for an advertisement

parts.note: a poster is a printed advertisement
a mast is a spar on a ship

explanation.surface: A spar appears in an advert for someone who looks after email.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar is a ship's pole here, not boxing practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Postmaster is the standard name for the administrator of a mail server who handles email problems.
